findings.criterion: 2 and 3 — pass verification and live-camera check-in correctness
findings.issue: LiveCamera invokes onQr and then continues the same frame's plate read; its stabilizer can invoke onPlate while the async pass lookup is pending. onPlate navigates away from CheckInCapture, but passErr is local to that unmounted screen. If lookup later rejects (including wrong-site/expired/invalid), applyPassError clears the persistent pending flag while setPassErr has nowhere visible to render. Confirm then has a plate, no pass, no error, and becomes enabled.
findings.consequence: An attendant who scanned an invalid pass can unknowingly submit the ordinary /v1/sessions walk-in branch, rather than seeing and verifying the rejection; the scanned pass workflow is silently bypassed and the stay can be treated incorrectly.
findings.correction: Prevent plate navigation while pass verification is pending, or persist lookup outcome/error in Flow and surface it on Review/Confirm. A rejected scan must remain visible and require an explicit return/acknowledgment before an ordinary walk-in can be submitted. Add a rendered deferred-lookup regression where QR and plate callbacks race, the lookup rejects after navigation, and no /v1/sessions request is possible until the rejection is handled.

findings.criterion: 1 — resident can actually share a usable QR pass
findings.issue: The no-Web-Share fallback awaits clipboard.writeText before creating/clicking the download anchor. If Clipboard exists but rejects (permission/policy/NotAllowedError), control jumps to the outer catch and the QR is never downloaded, leaving no share artifact. Current tests cover only the pure capability plan, not API rejection or the rendered share button/public guest route, and the recorded evidence explicitly says browser stories were not run.
findings.consequence: A reachable desktop/browser-policy branch reports sharing failed and gives the resident nothing to send; direct /pass rendering and scan-to-redeem also remain unverified in context.
findings.correction: Make QR download independent of clipboard success (catch clipboard failure separately and still download with honest status), add rendered coverage for file-share, text-share, clipboard success/rejection, and download-only branches, then open the emitted guest URL directly at a mobile viewport, decode/scan its rendered QR, and complete lookup/redeem.

findings.issue: The server contains a database verify_code comparison, but no recorded test reaches it. The existing forged-token and edited-version cases invalidate the HMAC first, so they establish signature rejection but not rejection of a still-valid signed token whose code no longer matches the stored verify_code. The acceptance prompt explicitly requires both protections to be verified by execution.
findings.consequence: Required executable evidence for the second tamper-protection layer is missing.
findings.correction: Add an API/service regression that issues a valid token, changes only the stored verify_code without changing qr_version (or otherwise constructs the valid-signature/stored-code-mismatch state), and proves lookup/redeem returns pass_invalid; retain the existing HMAC tamper assertions.

findings.criterion: 2 plus accessibility — scanned pass prepopulate, focus, edit, and redemption in context
findings.issue: The new executed-React test mounts only Flow and a counter probe. No executed component/browser path proves that a signed hinted pass fills the visible editable plate field, focuses/announces the accepted identity, survives edit/remove/replace, and submits /v1/passes/redeem with the persisted pass/plate association. The recorded evidence says these browser paths were not run.
findings.consequence: The acceptance-critical scan-to-prepopulated-form-to-verified-submit workflow remains unverified in the actual UI.
findings.correction: Add and run a rendered integration/browser story for hinted and no-hint passes, focus/live announcement, edit/remove/replace, and final redeem; assert the resulting session is associated with the intended pass and edited plate.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — camera scanning fills check-in and checkout plate fields
findings.issue: The existing fake-camera story covers only check-in and was not run; no checkout fake-camera story exists. Decoder/ALPR unit tests do not execute getUserMedia, React callbacks, controlled fields, route transitions, or checkout matching.
findings.consequence: Actual camera-to-field behavior remains unverified for both required workflows, with no execution evidence at all for checkout camera scanning.
findings.correction: Run and record the 390x844 fake-camera check-in story; add and run checkout coverage that opens a session, scans its plate, asserts the checkout plate field and correct match without manual entry, and records browser, fixture/model, viewport, and result.

findings.criterion: 5 plus authorization/UX — configurable overstay policy editor
findings.issue: GuestPasses enables policy inputs and Save with can('override'). The client maps override to supervisors as well as admins, while the server deliberately gives supervisors no settings.edit and protects PATCH /v1/pass-policy with that permission. A supervisor therefore sees an editable form whose save always fails. Separately, no rendered test changes the amount, saves, reloads, and observes persistence; the only browser story reads the default and was not run.
findings.consequence: The Settings UI misrepresents authorization and the required per-tenant policy edit/persistence path is not established end to end.
findings.correction: Gate editing on the exact settings/admin capability (for example me.superadmin || me.roles.includes('admin'), or expose settings.edit accurately), keep supervisor controls disabled/absent, and add a browser test proving admin save/reload persistence plus supervisor denial/no PATCH attempt.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 plus responsive authorization — Admin CRUD and Super Admin cross-property operations
findings.issue: The relevant browser stories were again explicitly not run. The CRUD story is desktop-only; the Super Admin story switches property but performs no edit/delete there; and no rendered test proves a regular administrator cannot read or mutate the second property.
findings.consequence: The required user-facing person/site/unit/slot CRUD, mobile usability, and cross-property authorization boundary remain unverified in context.
findings.correction: Run the existing stories; add representative person/site/unit/slot CRUD at a narrow mobile viewport, perform edit/delete after a Super Admin switches to a second property, and assert a regular administrator is denied that property's reads and mutations.
